result.title: IT policy: License hygiene and the waitlist
result.body:
When asked to run license hygiene for a product, do these in order.

**Reclaim** (`revoke_license`) the seats of:
- terminated employees;
- contractors whose `contract_end_date` is before today;
- active employees whose last activity was more than 60 days before today. Last activity is `last_active`, or
  `assigned_at` if `last_active` is empty.

Never reclaim from employees on leave, or for any other reason.

**Then work the waitlist:** open tickets tagged `waitlist:<product>` (`list_tickets`), oldest `opened_at` first. For
each ticket, in that order, until no seat is free:

- Requester terminated: set the ticket `declined`.
- Requester already holds a seat: set it `resolved`, without assigning anything.
- Otherwise the requester needs a `license` approval that counts (policy KB-P04).
  - If none counts, request one from the right approver now.
  - If the requester has one that counts, assign a seat and set the ticket `resolved`.
  - If their approval is still pending, set the ticket `pending_approval` and move on.

Once no seat is free, stop: leave every remaining waitlist ticket exactly as it is. Don't escalate purchases during
hygiene. Finally, set the conversation's own ticket `resolved`, with a note.

result.title: IT policy: Access: sensitivity and approvals
result.body:
Every group has a sensitivity: `standard`, `sensitive` or `privileged`.

**Nesting.** A group's `nested_in` lists the groups it is a member of. Members of a group are effectively members of
every group it is nested in, directly or through other groups. A group's **effective sensitivity** is the highest
sensitivity among the group itself and every group it is nested in, directly or indirectly. Use effective
sensitivity everywhere in this policy.

**Approvals needed before you add someone to a group (`add_to_group`):**

| Effective sensitivity | Approvals |
|---|---|
| standard | the employee's manager |
| sensitive | the employee's manager **and** the group owner |
| privileged | the employee's manager **and** Security |

- **Manager** means the employee's current manager (`manager_id` on the HR record), subject to policy KB-P05.
- **Group owner** means the group's `owner_id`, subject to policy KB-P05. If the employee receiving access is the group
  owner, the owner's manager approves in the owner's place (no one approves their own access).
- **Security** means any member of the group `security-approvers`.
- If one person fills two required roles, one approval from them covers both.
- Request every approval the access still needs at the same time, one request per approver.

**An approval counts only if all of these hold:**
1. Its status is `approved`.
2. Its type matches: `access` for groups, `license` for licenses, `sod_exception` for policy KB-P08, `hr_unlock` for
   policy KB-P07, `access_exception` for policy KB-P16.
3. It names the same employee (`subject_employee_id`) and the same group or product (`resource`).
4. It was decided within the last 14 days (`decided_at`). Exceptions (`access_exception`, `sod_exception`) are
   different: they count until their `valid_until` date, inclusive.
5. Its approver is the person this policy says must approve, as of now.
6. Its approver is not the employee receiving the access.

If an approval doesn't count, request a new one from the right person with `request_approval`. Approvers answer in the
approval system. If the answer is `pending`, tell the employee and leave the ticket `pending_approval` (policy KB-P14).

result.title: IT policy: Approvers who are away
result.body:
- If a person who must approve is on leave (`status: on_leave`), their delegate approves instead, but only if the
  delegation's `valid_from` to `valid_to` dates include today.
- If there is no valid delegate, that person's own manager approves instead, applying this rule again if needed.
- A terminated person can't approve. The person who was their manager (`manager_id`) approves instead, applying
  these rules again if needed.

Let me read the full current policy and the waitlist tickets.

Policy KB-P17 (current version) sets the rules. I'm reclaiming the seats that qualify: terminated employees, contractors past their end date, and active employees with no activity in 60+ days. Hollis Grant is on leave, so his seat stays. Lukas Brandvold's last activity was 59 days ago, which is under the 60-day threshold, so his seat stays too.

Five seats are free now. Next I'll check the license approvals for the waitlisted requesters in queue order.

Harriet Quill's approval was signed by herself, so I need to check whether it counts under the approval policy.

Several approvals don't count under KB-P04. Some were decided more than 14 days ago, some were signed by someone other than the requester's current manager, and Harriet's was self-approved. Before requesting replacements, I'll confirm the right approvers are active and not on leave.

Rosalind Ekberg (Fatima's manager) is on leave, and Marco Bianchi is her valid delegate. So Marco's approval for Fatima counts. Next I'll request the replacement approvals that are needed.

Now I'll assign seats in queue order. Aaron, Bianca, Fatima, Gideon and Harriet each have a counting approval, which gives five seats.

Seats are assigned. Now I'll update the waitlist tickets to match.

The DiagramPro hygiene run is done, and the waitlist has been worked in ticket order until the seats ran out.

**Seats reclaimed (5):**
- Corin Blake: terminated 2026-10-10
- Mads Iversen: contractor, contract ended 2026-09-30
- Priti Raman, Selma Okonjo, Ines Carvalho: active, no activity in 60+ days

**Lukas Brandvold's seat was not reclaimed.** His last activity was 2026-08-30, which is 59 days ago. Policy KB-P17 only allows reclaiming for inactivity over 60 days, and it doesn't allow reclaiming for other reasons. If he still hasn't used DiagramPro by about 2026-10-30, his seat becomes eligible and you can run the hygiene again then.

**Waitlist results:**
- **Assigned a seat and resolved (5):** T-7103 (Aaron Whitfield), T-7101 (Bianca Rossetti), T-7104 (Fatima Zahra Idrissi), T-7109 (Gideon Mwangi), T-7110 (Harriet Quill)
  - Fatima's manager is on leave, so her approval came from her delegate, Marco Bianchi.
  - Harriet's earlier approval was self-signed and didn't count, so I requested a new one from Sofia Andersson.
  - Bianca's earlier approval was more than 14 days old, so I requested a new one from Laura Bishop.
- **Declined (1):** T-7102 (Dorothea Klein), who was terminated 2026-10-21.
- **Resolved, no seat needed (1):** T-7106 (Emil Novotny), who already holds a seat.
- **Pending approval (1):** T-7107 (Chidi Okeke). His earlier approval came from Sofia, who isn't his manager. I requested one from Leah Whitman, who hasn't responded yet.
- **Still open, no seats left (2):** T-7105 (Isak Holmberg) and T-7108 (Juno Takahashi). Both have valid approvals, so they'll be served first if a seat frees up.

**Not touched:** Hollis Grant (E5204) is on leave until 2027-02-01, and policy never allows reclaiming from employees on leave, so his seat stays.

Your ticket T-6102 is resolved with a note covering all of this.
Thanks, that's a clear summary. Good to see the five seats freed up and the waitlist moving. I'll look at Lukas again around 2026-10-30 if he still hasn't opened it.

Sounds good. On 2026-10-30, Lukas's last activity will be more than 60 days old, so his seat will be eligible for reclaim if he still hasn't used DiagramPro. Just ask me to run the hygiene again then. T-7105 and T-7108 are still waiting for seats, and T-7107 is waiting on Leah Whitman's approval.
